findings.title: Raw HTML img sanitizing differs from what the PR says: it only runs when the setting is on, and srcset is never removed.
findings.body: The PR's security table says raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` when the setting is OFF, so `data:` images can't render. It also says `srcset` is removed in both states. In the code, the `Regex.Replace` only runs when `allowLocalImages` is true, so in the OFF state raw `` passes through unchanged. Nothing anywhere strips `srcset`. The regex also only matches double-quoted `src`. Single-quoted or unquoted `src` values (for example `src='https://evil/x.png'`) skip validation and never trigger the info bar. Either add the sanitizing for both states plus the `srcset` removal, or correct the security claims.

findings.title: No junction or symlink check, although the security model says reparse points are rejected.
findings.body: The PR says each part of the resolved path is rejected if it has `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`, because a lexical containment check doesn't stop redirection. Neither `TryResolveVirtualUrl` nor `TryGetLocalImageVirtualUrl` checks file attributes. They only compare `GetFullPath` and `GetRelativePath` results. A junction or symlink inside the document folder or share (for example `imgs` pointing to `C:\Users\victim`) passes the check, and the handler serves files from outside the allowed tree. Fix: before serving, walk each directory from the base path down to `resolvedPath` and reject any that has `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`, or compare against the final path from `FileSystemInfo.ResolveLinkTarget`.

findings.title: The raw HTML img rewrite only matches double-quoted src values.
findings.body: The pattern only matches `src="..."`. A local image written as `` or `` is never rewritten to the virtual host. It then resolves against the temp HTML file's location and is blocked, so the feature silently fails for valid HTML. A remote image written that way is blocked by the resource filter but never calls `imagesBlockedCallBack`, and with local images ON the regex-based info-bar check is skipped, so the user gets no notice. Fix: also match single-quoted and unquoted attribute values, or parse the HTML instead of using a regex.

findings.title: Any file under the base path is read fully into memory on the UI thread, with no limit on size or type.
findings.body: The handler serves any file the document points to, with no check on extension or size, and reads it with `File.ReadAllBytes` inside the WebResourceRequested callback. A Markdown file with `` or `![](backup.iso)` makes the preview host read gigabytes synchronously. With UNC paths the read also happens over the network. The preview pane hangs, and an `OutOfMemoryException` is not caught by the IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException handlers. Fix: only serve known image extensions (the ones `GetImageContentType` maps), refuse files above a reasonable size limit, and open a `FileStream` instead of buffering the whole file.

findings.title: Settings read only handles FileNotFoundException, so other failures break every Markdown preview.
findings.body: Before this change, the Markdown preview never read the PowerToys settings file. Now `GetLocalImagesEnabled()` runs on every preview and catches only `FileNotFoundException`. Two cases are not caught: a corrupt or half-written settings.json (`JsonException`), and a fresh profile where the settings folder doesn't exist yet (`DirectoryNotFoundException`, which is not a subclass of `FileNotFoundException`). Either one reaches `DoPreview` and the user gets the error page instead of the Markdown. I could not see `SettingsUtils.GetSettings`, so I can't tell which exceptions it already handles. Fix: use `GetSettingsOrDefault`, or catch `IOException` and `JsonException` (or `Exception`) and return `false`.
